summary: Iteration 6 backend smoke: full E2E verification of real YOLOv8n self-training pipeline. All 8 tests PASS (3m45s). Verified 30-image gate (400 with '30 labeled images' in detail), queued/real/yolov8n job creation, status progression queued->preparing->training->trained, GET /models/{mid} polling, weights_path + final_mAP/precision/recall populated on completion, activate 400 when not yet trained, activation sets is_active on THIS model and clears others (single-active), auto-label returns source='model' after activation with boxes, source='gemini' fallback for projects with no active model, GET /projects/{pid}/models still lists real+other, batch auto-label writes source_counts={model,gemini} on batch_jobs.

minor.issue: Payload schema BatchAutoLabelIn accepts only {only_unlabeled: bool} - no way to explicitly pass image_ids (contract description in review request implied image_ids). Works fine via only_unlabeled=True but callers cannot restrict to a subset.

Uses FastAPI BackgroundTasks bound to the request - long-running YOLO training (minutes) blocks the request's background task lifecycle; on uvicorn worker restart mid-training the job stays 'training' forever with no watchdog. Consider a dedicated worker/queue.
Downloads yolov8n.pt to backend cwd on first call (ultralytics does this). First training run in a fresh pod pays a network + write penalty; consider pre-bundling yolov8n.pt at /app/backend/.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1987 lines — long overdue to split into feature routers (auth/projects/images/annotations/review/comments/notifications/models/batch/teams).
_train_yolo_sync uses synchronous PyMongo inside asyncio.to_thread — OK but note ObjectId leaks if any downstream code reads without projection; current code updates by 'id' only so safe.

activate_model deactivates ALL prior models including simulated ones in the same project — matches spec (single-active), but consider also emitting an activity/notification event beyond _log_activity for observability.

_auto_label_router falls back to Gemini on ANY inference exception (including transient GPU/thread errors) — could silently degrade quality. Consider a retry-once policy for local inference before falling back.
MIN_TRAINING_IMAGES=30 is hardcoded; expose via env or per-project config for flexibility.
No pagination or lifecycle cleanup on db.models — over time inactive/failed models accumulate per project.

Weights are pulled from object storage every time _load_yolo is called for a fresh weights_path (cached in-process dict only). On multi-worker uvicorn deployments the cache is per-worker so cold-inference latency will spike. Consider a shared local file cache under /tmp keyed by weights_path hash.
train_real endpoint accepts arbitrary epochs (default 30) with no upper bound — could DoS the pod. Cap at e.g. 200.
test_credentials: Test self-registers TEST_rt_<uuid>@vf.io/pw12345 users per module. demo@vf.io/demo1234 also present.
seed_data_creation: Per-test-run: 1 fresh user, 2 projects (one 'small' with 3 approved+annotated images for the 400-gate test, one 'big' with 32 approved+annotated synthetic images (red rects + blue circles) used for actual YOLOv8 training + activation + inference). Training runs at epochs=3, imgsz=640, batch=8, CPU — ~3min end-to-end on this pod. Not cleaned up (matches prior iterations).
context_for_next_testing_agent: real_training_smoke.py exercises the full pipeline including a real 3-epoch YOLOv8n training that takes ~3-4 minutes on CPU. Tests use module-scoped fixtures and stash rt_model_id/rt_trained_doc on pytest module for cross-test state. Prior smoke suites (backend_smoke.py, teams_smoke.py, annotator_v2_smoke.py, review_batch_smoke.py, collab_smoke.py) were NOT re-run this iteration but per iteration_5 report were fully green. Public URL https://ai-vision-hub-20.preview.emergentagent.com occasionally throttles bursty uploads; the test uses urllib3 Retry(total=5, backoff=1.5) — recommend keeping that pattern in future tests.
rca of the issue: No functional issues detected. Initial test run had connect timeouts to the public URL during a 32-image upload burst; adding session-level HTTPAdapter retries fixed it and the second run completed all 8 tests including full training in 3m45s. Root cause of the transient timeouts was ingress-level connection pressure, not the backend.
